evals.name: unknown-compatibility-handoff
evals.prompt: Delete a public camelCase query alias. Existing clients may still send it, and no supported-client evidence, migration policy, or ADR has been checked.
evals.expected_output: Stop deletion and hand the unknown compatibility policy and required authority to design.
assertions: Names engineering-design-thinking as the next owner
Carries caller gaps, policy choice, authority, and rollback need
Does not delete or rewrite tests to bless the removal

evals.name: multiple-candidates-handoff
evals.prompt: Clean up catalog architecture, but three competing module end states remain and none has been ranked or selected.
evals.expected_output: Stop execution and hand the candidate evidence to architecture review for discovery and prioritization.
assertions: Does not pick an end state
Names improve-arch-go as the next owner
Carries candidate scope and available evidence
Does not start cleanup before one candidate is accepted

evals.name: behavior-change-handoff
evals.prompt: The cleanup is approved, but one slice will intentionally change an observable response and fix a client-facing bug. The desired behavior is settled.
evals.expected_output: Pause cleanup and hand the accepted behavior delta to a RED-GREEN implementation slice, returning only for remaining structural work.
assertions: Names tdd-go as the next owner
Carries the accepted behavior delta and current invariants
Defines return only after behavior is green

evals.name: accepted-cleanup-entry
evals.prompt: Remove one obsolete internal adapter. The end state, scope, invariants, compatibility evidence, and decision authority are approved; behavior must remain unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Own the bounded cleanup, preserve tests after each reversible slice, and avoid unnecessary design or TDD phases.
assertions: Treats zero-tech-debt as the current owner
Does not auto-run all linked skills
Preserves verified behavior while deleting the accepted path
